subject: Kokoro decoder length buckets (lean masking)
method: Inputs are zero-padded to the smallest bucket >= frames and noise extends the same seeded sequence. Length-dependent work is confined to the valid prefix: InstanceNorm statistics (one pass of sum x and sum x*x over valid positions, affine folded into a per-channel gain and shift, output masked to exact zeros), the reverse LSTM direction, the F0 phase interpolation edge (last valid value held), the harmonic STFT end reflection (10 samples written at the valid end), and the iSTFT frames and envelope. Because LeakyReLU and Snake map 0 to 0, conv inputs after a masked norm already equal zero padding; only transposed-conv outputs and the generator stage inputs are masked again.

cases.name: speed-bf_emma
cases.note: bucket already specialized by the previous case

native.cold_cache_isolation: Exported minutes before the run and never specialized, so each bucket's first use is a genuine cold specialization. No shared cache was cleared or redirected; Core AI exposes no per-process cache directory.
native.lifecycle: cancellation recovery and active unload bit-identical; frames exact; repeats identical

paired_timing.protocol: one process per shape, all three decoders loaded and warmed, 9 interleaved rounds; median seconds per warm decode on the GPU (load averages 26-36)

padded_1024_valid_913_vs_unbucketed_913.note: minimums 0.51 vs 0.65; padding to the bucket costs at most the bucket ratio

paired_timing.finding: The first masking's cost was in the decomposed two-pass norm statistics and the extra masking around every norm and conv, which multiplied large-tensor kernel count. Single-pass masked statistics with folded affine and masked norm output, plus relying on zero-preserving activations, bring the bucketed decoder to parity with the unbucketed one at the same shape while staying exact.

lean_bucketed_sweep.footprint_mib: flat within buckets up to 1024 (about 4.2 GB); 6.2-12.4 GB fluctuating within bucket 2048

memory.unload_note: Footprint sampled immediately after unload was 0.33 GB in one bucketed run and 8.5 GB in the other: the framework's allocator caches are not returned deterministically at that instant. Metal allocation after unload stayed about 8.2 GB in both, so MPSGraph keeps some per-process caches past model release.
memory.scope: phys_footprint from task_info(TASK_VM_INFO) and MTLDevice.currentAllocatedSize of the default device, sampled after each call
memory.guidance: Bucket 2048 alone adds about 8.3 GB of Metal allocation. Cap segments at 1024 frames (about 25 s) where memory matters; on iOS cap the maximum bucket at what the device fits and refuse longer segments.
